info.name: EasyAgric API
info.description: Agricultural advisory app — soil analysis, weather, crop recommendations.

variable.description: JWT access token — populated automatically after Login or Register
JWT refresh token — populated automatically after Login or Register
Target user id for the Admin — User Management requests
Populated automatically after declaring or recording a payment

request.description: Returns all supported language codes and names. No authentication required. The Flutter app should call this on first launch to populate the language picker.

Creates a farmer account. No password — a secure password is auto-generated and emailed to the farmer. Returns JWT access and refresh tokens. Supported language codes: en, fr, sw, ha, yo, ig, am, zu, xh, tw, wo, ln, sn, dyu, bci, bm, ff. Defaults to 'en' if omitted.
Authenticates any user (farmer, app manager, or admin). Returns JWT access token (30 min) and refresh token (7 days).
Exchange a refresh token for a new access token. The old refresh token is blacklisted and a new one is returned (token rotation). Call this when the access token expires.
Creates an App Manager account. Requires superadmin authentication. A secure password is auto-generated and emailed. App managers can access all endpoints without GPS coordinates.

Returns the authenticated user's profile: id, email, role, phone, farm_name, date_joined, and `subscription` (plan, status, days_remaining, analyses_remaining). `subscription` is null for admins and app managers, who are not metered.
Partially updates the authenticated user's profile. All fields are optional.
Changes the password for the authenticated user. Requires the current password for verification. Returns fresh JWT tokens so the user stays logged in after the change.
Sends a 6-digit OTP to the email. Valid for 10 minutes. Always returns the same message (prevents user enumeration).
Verifies the OTP and sets a new password. Returns fresh JWT tokens.

query.description: GPS latitude (captured by mobile app at the farm)
GPS longitude (captured by mobile app at the farm)

request.description: Returns current weather, soil temperature at 0/6/18/54 cm depth, soil moisture, and 7-day forecast from Open-Meteo. Requires authentication. lat and lon are required for farmers; admins and app managers receive a prompt if omitted.

formdata.description: Photo of the soil taken by the farmer at the farm

request.description:
Upload a soil photo. Gemini Vision analyses it and returns soil type, color, texture, pH estimate, fertility, visible issues, and amendment recommendations.

Consumes one analysis credit, but only if the analysis succeeds. Returns 402 Payment Required when the trial has expired or its 5 analyses are used up — the body carries a machine-readable `code` (expired | quota_exhausted | cancelled) and the current subscription. Admins and app managers are never metered.

query.description: Clay | Sandy | Loam | Silt | Laterite | Black Cotton | Alluvial
Current air temperature in °C (optional — improves ranking)

request.description: Returns crops ranked by suitability for the given soil type and current temperature. Factors in the current month for seasonal filtering.

formdata.description: Photo of the soil taken at the farm
GPS latitude — captured automatically by the mobile app at the farm
GPS longitude — captured automatically by the mobile app at the farm

request.description:
Main mobile endpoint. Farmer takes a soil photo at their farm — the mobile app captures GPS automatically. Returns soil analysis, weather data, and crop recommendations in one response. Report is also emailed to the farmer and a push notification is sent. Admins and app managers can omit lat/lon — weather will be skipped but soil analysis still runs.

Consumes one analysis credit, and only if the soil analysis succeeds — a Gemini failure costs the farmer nothing. Returns 402 Payment Required once the 14-day / 5-analysis trial is exhausted; see Subscriptions & Payments.
Returns all analysis records for the authenticated farmer, ordered by most recent first.
Returns full detail of a single analysis record. Replace 1 with the actual record id.
Returns aggregate stats: total farmers, new farmers (7/30 days), total analyses, analyses (7/30 days). Requires admin or app manager role.
Returns all farmers with their analysis count, ordered by most recently joined. Requires admin or app manager role.
Returns a farmer's profile and their 10 most recent analyses. Replace 1 with the actual farmer id. Requires admin or app manager role.
Registers the device's FCM token for push notifications. Call this on app launch after the user logs in. platform must be 'android' or 'ios'.
Removes the device token. Call this on logout so the user no longer receives push notifications on this device.

item.name: Subscriptions & Payments
item.description:
Every farmer gets a 14-day trial capped at 5 soil analyses when they register. After that, /advisor/ and /soil/analyze/ return 402 until a paid plan is activated.

There is no payment gateway: farmers pay in cash or by bank transfer and a human confirms it. A farmer-declared transfer lands as `pending` and unlocks nothing until staff confirm it; a payment recorded by an admin or app manager is confirmed on creation, because they are holding the money.

request.description: Public. Lists every plan with its duration in days and included analysis quota (null quota = unlimited). Prices are NOT here — they are per-currency, see Get Payment Instructions.

Current plan, status, days_remaining and analyses_remaining for the logged-in farmer. Use this to drive the paywall screen in the app.

`pending_upgrade` holds the plan the farmer has requested but staff have not confirmed yet (null when there is none) — show it as 'Pro — awaiting confirmation'.

query.description: XOF | XAF | NGN | GHS | KES | UGX | TZS | RWF | ZAR | ETB | USD | EUR. Defaults to DEFAULT_CURRENCY.

request.description:
Everything the farmer needs in order to pay: the price of each plan in this currency, the bank account to transfer to, and who to hand cash to.

Returns 404 with `available_currencies` if nothing is priced in the requested currency — a fresh deploy must be seeded first (`manage.py seed_payment_config`).

The farmer asks to move onto a paid plan BEFORE paying — no reference or receipt needed, `method` is only how they intend to pay.

Nothing activates: the farmer stays on their current plan and the paywall stays shut until an admin or app manager calls Confirm Payment. The response returns `amount_due` and the bank account, so the app can show how to pay on the same screen.

Sending a new request replaces a previous un-evidenced one, so a farmer can change their mind. A transfer already declared with a reference is left alone for staff to rule on.

Saves the pending payment id into {{payment_id}}.

The farmer reports a transfer they have already made. Lands as `pending` and changes nothing until staff confirm it.

`amount` is optional — it defaults to the list price (price x months). A smaller amount is accepted but flagged to staff via `shortfall`. A bank transfer needs either a `reference` or a receipt photo; to send a photo instead, switch the body to form-data with fields plan, method, currency and a `proof` file.

Saves the new payment id into {{payment_id}}.

Admin / app manager only. An agent who collected cash in the field records it against the farmer's account (`email` or `user_id`).

Because the agent is holding the money, this is CONFIRMED immediately — the plan activates and the farmer is emailed, with no second review step. A farmer calling this for someone else gets 403.
Farmers see only their own payments; admins and app managers see everyone's. Filter by `status=pending` for the daily queue of transfers waiting to be checked against the bank statement.

Admin / app manager only. Confirms the money arrived: activates the plan for the requested number of months, resets the analysis counter, and emails the farmer in their own language.

Returns the updated subscription. Confirming twice returns 400.
Admin / app manager only. The plan is left untouched and the farmer is emailed the reason. A payment that is already confirmed cannot be rejected (400) — adjust it in Django admin instead.

Admin / app manager only. Moves a farmer onto a paid plan WITHOUT recording a payment — for complimentary accounts, goodwill extensions or fixing a mistake. Normal paid signups should go through the payment endpoints so the money is auditable.

Identify the farmer by `email` or `user_id`. `months` and `analysis_quota` are optional and default to the plan's configuration.

item.name: Admin — User Management
item.description:
Platform admins only (role `admin`, or a Django superuser). App managers are deliberately excluded — `is_privileged` is too broad for destructive account operations.

Deleting a user is permanent and cascades to their subscription, payments, analysis history and device tokens. Prefer Deactivate unless the account really must be erased.

query.description: farmer | admin | appmanager — omit for every account
Partial match on email or farm name

request.description:
Find the account to act on — this is where you read the `id` used by Preview, Deactivate and Delete.

Returns {count, limit, offset, results}, newest first. `count` is the total matching your filters, not the size of the page, so you can always tell when more accounts exist.

Filters: `role` (farmer | admin | appmanager), `is_active` (true | false), `search` (matches email OR farm name, partial).
Paging: `limit` (default 100, max 500), `offset`.

Each row carries id, email, role, phone, farm_name, language, is_active, date_joined, last_login and current `plan` (null for staff, who are not metered).

Shows the account plus `deletion_impact` — exactly how many rows would be destroyed with it, per model. Computed from Django's own deletion collector, so it stays accurate as the schema grows.

Always worth calling before Delete User.

The reversible option, and the right one in most cases. The account can no longer log in, but the farmer's history and payment records are preserved. Send `is_active: true` to restore access.

Admins cannot deactivate themselves.

query.description: Required only to delete an account that has confirmed payments

request.description:
PERMANENT. Removes the account and everything cascading from it — subscription, payments, analysis history, device tokens. The response reports what was destroyed.

Guardrails:
- 400 if you target your own account. This is what stops the platform being locked out: the caller is an admin and cannot remove themselves, so an admin always survives.
- 409 if the account has confirmed payments, since deleting it would erase financial records. Deactivate instead, or repeat with ?force=true to go ahead anyway.

Payments this user *recorded or reviewed* as staff are not deleted — those links are set to null, so the farmer's payment history survives.

item.name: Products
item.description:
Catalogue of agricultural products listed in the app — 48 entries seeded from `apps/products/data/products.json` via `manage.py seed_products`.

Two kinds share one catalogue: `input` (seeds, fertiliser, crop protection, tools, irrigation, protective gear) and `produce` (grains, tubers, legumes, vegetables, fruits, cash crops). Images ship empty — upload a file in Django admin or set `image_url`.

query.description: input | produce — omit for the whole catalogue
seed | fertilizer | crop_protection | tool | irrigation | protective_equipment | grain | tuber | legume | vegetable | fruit | cash_crop
Partial match on name or description

request.description:
Returns {count, limit, offset, results}. Each row: id, slug, name, kind, kind_display, category, category_display, description, unit, image, image_credit.

`image` is a single resolved URL, picked in order: a real photo uploaded in Django admin, then the freely-licensed photo URL, then a generated placeholder card. It is never null.

`image_credit` carries the attribution the photo's licence requires (mostly CC BY-SA) — display it wherever the image is shown. It is empty for generated cards. Only active products are listed.
Drives the filter chips. Returns the categories grouped under each kind, each with a live product count — so the app never shows a filter that would come back empty.
Single product by slug (slugs are generated from the name, e.g. `cocoa`, `hybrid-maize-seed`, `knapsack-sprayer-16-l`). 404 if the slug is unknown or the product is inactive.
